_comment: Labelled gold set for the M9/M10 screening judgments.
Used two ways: tests/unit/test_jev_screening.py measures the keyword
baseline offline (no key, no network), and tests/smoke/test_jev_screening.py
measures Jev against the same cases and asserts it beats that baseline.
Cases were chosen to include the failure modes substring matching cannot
handle: negation, bare-word coincidence, and topics that share vocabulary
but differ in what the proposal actually asks for. The `note` on each case
says what it is testing. Extend this file rather than loosening a floor.

proposal_topics.text: RESOLVED: Shareholders request the Board report on the effectiveness of the Company's supplier auditing program in detecting forced labor in tier-2 facilities.
proposal_topics.note: plain case; keyword table gets this

proposal_topics.text: RESOLVED: Shareholders request an annual report on the Company's greenhouse gas emissions across Scope 1, 2 and 3, with targets aligned to the Paris Agreement.
RESOLVED: Shareholders request the Compensation Committee report on the alignment between CEO pay and the Company's median worker pay ratio.
RESOLVED: Shareholders request the Board report on the Company's political contributions and trade association dues, including payments used for lobbying.
RESOLVED: Shareholders request an annual report on the Company's workforce diversity data, disaggregated by gender and race at each job category.
RESOLVED: Shareholders request the Board adopt a policy requiring shareholder approval before the Company issues shares representing more than 20% of outstanding stock.
RESOLVED: Shareholders request the Board amend the bylaws to permit holders of 10% of outstanding shares to call a special meeting.

RESOLVED: Shareholders request the Board report on risks arising from the Company's use of arbitration clauses in employment contracts, including their effect on workers' ability to pursue harassment claims.
proposal_topics.note: about the company's own workforce; contains no word from the worker_welfare list

proposal_topics.text: RESOLVED: Shareholders request a report on the human rights impacts of the Company's operations on communities near its own facilities, excluding supplier operations.
proposal_topics.note: explicitly excludes suppliers; keyword table fires supply_chain on 'human rights'

proposal_topics.text: RESOLVED: Shareholders request a report assessing whether the Company's lobbying on climate policy is consistent with its stated emissions targets.
proposal_topics.note: ambiguous by design; the ask is about lobbying alignment, not emissions. Keyword table fires environmental first

proposal_topics.text: RESOLVED: Shareholders request the Board report on pay equity across gender and racial groups within the Company's workforce.
proposal_topics.note: contains 'pay'; keyword table may fire executive_pay

proposal_topics.text: RESOLVED: Shareholders request the Board report on the Company's efforts to reduce injury rates among warehouse staff, including audit findings from third-party safety inspectors.
proposal_topics.note: contains 'audit'; keyword table fires supply_chain first

proposal_topics.text: RESOLVED: Shareholders request the Board report on the Company's water usage and discharge permits at its manufacturing sites.
proposal_topics.note: no keyword from the environmental list appears

proposal_topics.text: RESOLVED: Shareholders request the Company disclose the total compensation of its five most highly paid non-executive employees.
proposal_topics.note: explicitly non-executive; 'compensation' pulls the keyword table to executive_pay

proposal_topics.text: RESOLVED: Shareholders request the Board report on the Company's process for verifying that cobalt in its products is not mined with child labor.

merger_factors.target: A regional hospital system operating twelve acute-care facilities.
merger_factors.deal: The acquirer, a national health insurer, will integrate the target's provider network with its existing health plan membership.
merger_factors.note: plain case; keyword table gets this

merger_factors.target: An independent e-commerce seller of household goods.
merger_factors.deal: The acquirer operates the online marketplace on which the target currently sells, and will bring the target's catalogue in-house.

merger_factors.target: A manufacturer of consumer electronics accessories.
merger_factors.deal: The acquirer does not operate a marketplace and has no insurance business. The two companies serve entirely separate customer bases with numerous alternative suppliers available.
merger_factors.note: negation; keyword table fires platform_plus_seller and payer_plus_provider on the denial itself

merger_factors.target: A commercial landscaping business with operations in four states.
merger_factors.deal: The acquirer will fund the transaction partly through proceeds from a life insurance policy held on its founder.
merger_factors.note: bare-word coincidence; 'insurance' alone scores 1.5 of 9.0 under the keyword table

merger_factors.deal: The acquirer owns the only rail terminal serving the corridor, which the target's competitors must use to reach the port.
merger_factors.note: the economic theory is present but none of the bottleneck keywords appear

merger_factors.deal: The acquirer is a pharmacy benefit manager that sets the formulary tiers determining reimbursement for the target's products, and also owns a competing generics business.

merger_factors.target: A regional grocery chain with 8% share of a fragmented market.
merger_factors.deal: The combined entity would face numerous competitors; the pre-merger HHI in the served market is 1,150.
merger_factors.note: numeric HHI below threshold; must not trigger

merger_factors.deal: Post-merger HHI in the relevant market is estimated at 3,400, up from 2,900 pre-merger.
merger_factors.note: numeric HHI above threshold; arithmetic, owned by code
